newsitem.title: USA: Shoreham-Wading River CSD, N.Y., TANs SP-1 - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Shoreham-Wading River CSD, N.Y., TANs SP-1 - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 17 - Standard & Poor's Corp Tuesday said it has assigned its SP-1' rating to Shoreham-Wading River Central School District, N.Y.'s TANs series 1996 due June 25, 1997.
- Strong net cash coverage of note debt service at maturity,

- An agreement between the district and the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) regarding the amount and timing of payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) to be made by LIPA to the Town of Brookhaven on behalf of the district,
- Statutory provisions requiring any potential tax refund payment to be made by the district no earlier than the district's fiscal 1998 budget, and
- The uncertainty resulting from current and future litigation regarding property assessments for the Shoreham Nuclear Power Station (Shoreham).

Under New York local finance law, whenever the amount of the TANs outstanding equals the amount of property taxes to be collected, the district is required to segregate such taxes in a separate note repayment account. In addition, the notes represent a general obligation of the district. Net cash coverage of debt service at note maturity by projected available cash balances is strong at 1.7 times.

Pursuant to an agreement dated Sept. 11, 1996 between LIPA and the respective municipalities involved, including the district, LIPA has agreed to make payments in lieu of taxes to the Town of Brookhaven on behalf of the municipalities as follows: $24.5 million on or before Sept. 1, 1996 and $24.5 million on or before March 1, 1997. The district's share of those payments includes $9.6 million received in September 1996 and $8.0 million to be distributed in March 1996. The PILOT payments represent 59% of the district's total general fund revenues for fiscal year 1997.

Currently, the district's potential liability resulting from the litigation surrounding Shoreham is estimated to be $28 million and potential gains total $52 million. These judgments are in various states in the appeals process and the district is currently negotiating with all parties to reach an overall settlement. However, in the event that a determination of liability is made during the 1997 fiscal year, under state law, any refund of tax payments would not have to be paid by the district until the 1998 fiscal year, subsequent to note maturity, Standard & Poor's said.
